sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section provides the header and date for the maamar.

translations.translation: With the help of Heaven.
Monday, Parshat Eikev,
the fifteenth of Av, 5747*

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the greatness of the fifteenth of Av lies in the ascent after the descent of Tisha B'Av, making its lunar fullness superior to that of other months.

translations.translation: “There were no better days for Israel than the fifteenth of Av and Yom Kippur.”
And the Rebbe
(the Rebbe Rashab)
of blessed memory, in his maamar explaining the concept of the fifteenth of Av,
brings what is stated in Pri Etz Chaim
that the festival of the fifteenth of Av is when there is the perfection
of the filling of the moon.
[And the events that occurred on the fifteenth of Av
(listed in the Gemara)
are like results of the essential concept of this day – the perfection of the filling of the moon.]
And the maamar notes precisely:
Now, that on the fifteenth day the moon stands in its fullness
occurs every month,
and nevertheless, festivals were not established for it except for Pesach
(the fifteenth of Nissan)
and Sukkot
(the fifteenth of Tishrei).
And even more so, it is not understood,
that from the simple language of “there were no better days for Israel than the fifteenth of Av etc.” it implies that it is a greater festival than all the festivals,
even from the festivals of Pesach and Sukkot,
even though these festivals are also on the fifteenth of the month.
And the point of the explanation of this
(in the maamar) is,
that the essential advantage of the filling and perfection of the moon on this fifteenth day is that the filling and perfection comes after a lack,
for after a lack, the perfection is a loftier perfection than the perfection that is intrinsic,
as is known
the principle regarding ascents and descents,
that the ascent after a descent is an ascent to a level higher than the level before the descent,
and the greater the descent,
the greater the ascent.
And therefore, the essential advantage of the filling of the moon is on the fifteenth of Av,
for in the month of Av,
the descent of the moon
(and Israel, who are compared to the moon)
is a very great descent,
and therefore the ascent of the fifteenth of Av
(which follows the descent of Tisha B'Av)
is a very great ascent.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section connects the festival of the fifteenth of Av to the cessation of the deaths of the generation of the wilderness, illustrating the ascent after the descent of Tisha B'Av and hinting at the future redemption.

translations.translation: B)
And it can be said,

that the aforementioned concept, that the festival of the fifteenth of Av is because then is the ascent after the descent of Tisha B'Av, is also hinted at in that the first event that occurred on the fifteenth of Av was that the generation of the wilderness ceased to die.
For the concept of the generation of the wilderness is connected with Tisha B'Av,
for on Tisha B'Av it was decreed upon the generation of the wilderness that they would die in the wilderness and not enter the Land,
and also the fulfillment of the decree was on Tisha B'Av,
for on every Tisha B'Av
(of the last thirty-nine years that they were in the wilderness)
they would dig their graves.
And the festival of the fifteenth of Av, on which the generation of the wilderness ceased to die, is the ascent after the descent of Tisha B'Av.
And from this it is also understood regarding
(the essential)
descent of Tisha B'Av, on which the Temple was destroyed, the First and the Second,
[and particularly, since the decree of the destruction was also on that same day
(Tisha B'Av of the first year that they were in the wilderness)
on which it was decreed upon the generation of the wilderness that they would not enter the Land,
and both decrees were for the same sin
(the sin of the spies)],
that on the fifteenth of Av, a glimmer of the revelation of the future shines,
whose essence
is the building of the Third Temple
– the ascent after the descent of the destruction of the First and Second Temples.
